STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple sitting on a white square plate, photographed from directly above (top-down view). It is a snack, not a full meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is about 22 cm across (similar to a side/salad plate). Plate area ≈ 22 x 22 x 0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm^2. The apple itself is about 7.5 cm in diameter, which fits that scale.

STEP 3 - Items: One red-and-yellow apple (whole, unpeeled).

STEP 4 - Area: Apple footprint ≈ 3.14 x (3.75)^2 ≈ 44 cm^2, which is about 11% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: The apple is roughly spherical, so its volume is about 4/3 x 3.14 x 3.75^3 ≈ 220 ml. Using the footprint and height gives a similar envelope, so I keep ~220 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit has a bulk density of roughly 0.6-0.7 g/ml when treated as a pile, but a single whole apple is nearly solid. Its real mass is about 170-180 g (a medium apple). I use the physical estimate of ~170 g, which is consistent with the volume once the hollow stem area and air around it are counted.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple, raw, with skin ≈ 52 kcal per 100 g. 170 g x 0.52 ≈ 88 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at ~170 g and ~90 kcal is plausible for a single visible apple on a small plate. The plate itself is not food and is not counted.
